utterances.text: [Interpretation] The guard who was standing in front of me opened fire, and I remember that somebody grabbed the barrel and pointed it into the air. But the one who did this knew these people. I think that they all knew each other. Some of them even said, Fuck it, it's a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First, you were taken to Miska Glava?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No. We were first taken to a meadow where we were assembled. And somebody threw a stone at us. And then, in the meantime, a van arrived, and it took us to Miska Glava in several batches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many people could be accommodated in the van?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We were packed, as many as possible. It -- it was not according to the standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now you arrived at Miska Glava.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the Dom.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what kind of uniforms did you see there?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Olive-drab-green.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see people in reserve police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just refresh your memory by looking at the transcript tendered by the Prosecution. We need P998 in e-court, page 17 in the English. We did not operate with the B/C/S version at all because we were not aware of there being one. You were asked by the Prosecutor - for the record that's page 5219 from the Stakic transcript: [In English] "Were there people in uniforms? Could you tell who they were or what units they were from?" And your answer was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What line are you reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, 16 and further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And your answer was: "I think it was the Miska Glava Territorial Defence, and they were wearing JNA uniforms. I didn't see any other kind of uniforms in that place, although at the place where we were taken prisoner, there were also reserve police uniforms."

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So at the place where you were detained, men were dressed in reserve police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember. What do you mean, military police?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the meadow where we were captured or -- what are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I read it out to you where you said that, at that place where we were incarcerated, there were men in reserve police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it seems that we're talking about the Dom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Lukic, it was translated to us your question as incarcerated which seems to refer to a detention situation. Could we clearly distinguish between --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But also in such a way that witness is not confused. In this transcript the witness refers to reserve police uniforms at the location where he was taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Prisoner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- prisoner. Yes. And that is not where he was incarcerated but where he was taken prisoner. Incarceration follows once you have been taken prisoner, taken to a place and then that may be a different place and that may have been, for example, the Miska Glava -- the Miska Glava Dom. So could we clearly distinguish between the two. Please proceed. I leave it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karagic, do you remember now you were imprisoned in Miska Glava Dom. Around the Dom, did you see that a delegation arrived in light brown uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: It is possible. Yes, there was a delegation. Now whether they were dressed in uniforms, but it was that colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Light brown?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, probably. It's been 20 years. But I think it's more like coffee brown.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also saw, but that was at the stadium later, Becir Stojan who was dressed in black; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I think it was him. Whether it was him --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but anyway you saw a man --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw a man on the bus also dressed in black. But that was another person. And this one with a beard resembles most Stojan Becir. I happened to see his picture in the "Blic" or in another newspaper when he was arrested, so I put two and two together, and he also had a cross around his neck so it must have been him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He had a beard?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, a well-trim beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the Miska Glava Dom, where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: From the Dom?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: We were taken to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I again ask you, Witness, to make a short pause between question and answer. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I have forgotten again that this needs to be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not the only one who forgets now and then. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The stadium is situated between Gornja Ljubija and Donja Ljubija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this is where you were lined up. How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: While we were passing through Ljubija, when I saw the army there, a man in black uniform came in, and he asked about people with my last name, and I remember my father telling me to keep quiet. One of the guys wanted to say, Now, what do you want? And he started slapping him across the face or kicking him. And then at the very entrance to the stadium when we reached it, we got off, running, and people were waiting for us. There was a bus driver with a moustache and he was beating us. So when I arrived there, it seemed to me that there had been people there before we arrived. There were many of us, so they made two lines along the wall the -- the length of the stadium. But I don't know how many people there were exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they put -- put you in two lines or in four lines?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, two lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we briefly see one portion ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the last part of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're invited to repeat the last part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at document 1D182 [as interpreted]. It's the witness's statement given the Prosecution on the 10th of November, 1998. We need paragraph 5. It's page 3 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's 1D812.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Lawyer. Does my statement say that I said four lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't believe I ever said that, just like about the thing a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the middle of this paragraph, it says -- so what you think that what you stated at the time that you were lined up in four lines that is not correct?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't believe I ever said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. And, now, in front of the stadium where you were lined up, what kind of uniforms did you observe there?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: At the moment, all I can remember is this major in an olive-drab uniform. Maybe with a white belt. Maybe his uniform was with a pattern. I cannot confirm. I don't know. The one who was addressed as Vojvoda, who I think it was actually Stojan Becir, that he was in civilian clothes. He was in black anyway, but whether it was civilian clothes or not, I don't know. And whether it was Stojan Becir or not, all I can say is I presume it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you see a policeman there?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe the one with the white belt was supposed to be some kind of military policeman; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. A moment ago you mentioned something and I'd like to go back to that now. Actually, we'll go back in time. When you were taken prisoner in this forest was called it Kalajevo or Kurevo?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Kalajevo. You mean where we were taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Kalajevo, and then we were running, running, and now where we were when we were taken prisoner, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. But just before that, I was just wondering whether it was Kurevo?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I mean, to this day I don't know what belongs to Kurevo. I know that they called this Kalajevo where we were taken this rest. Now where we ran, I know that we crossed some road and whatever and I don't know how much time went by as we were running. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also say that they found something on a man -- or rather, in this man's pocket, or did he throw this out of his pocket?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: A little pistol. He threw it out of his pocket as if it had been handmade and also a knife, and then they wanted to slit the throat of -- well. But anyway, he started running away and I've already said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. You've already said that. In one statement, you mention a penknife and in another statement you mention a small pistol. Today you're saying both.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Who said anything different?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're going to look at this briefly now. 1D --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: You know, you know, I mean, I never really said what the man had in his pocket. I said what was on the pile. Now whether it belonged to the same man, I don't know. I know there was some pistol and this penknife, knife, whatever you call it. Well, it was small anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not catch the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wanted to slit his throat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. The interpreters did not catch the last part. You said, "I know there was some" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You said: "I know there was some pistol and this penknife, knife, whatever you call it ... it was small anyway." What did you then add after you said, "It was small anyway"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I said that I never claimed that it was in his pocket that it was found in his pocket. It was in front of us. Us as a group. Not in somebody's pocket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Miska Glava, where was it that you were actually detained?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a sort of coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it within this Dom?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you came to the Dom, did they write down your names?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now was it immediately or -- no. I think it was during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did they give you water in Miska Glava?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that. It's already stated there. Well, there was this old man, a nice old man -- well, he was good. He was nice. He gave us water when we were there with him. And afterwards, at day break, the old man was no longer there. Then it was bad, because we had to sing in order to get water, whatever, and then when we'd go out, we'd get beaten up, and if somebody went out to piss, take a piss - I'm sorry for using this kind of word - also we were sort of afraid to go out. I went out to urinate. They didn't mistreat me. But they sure did mistreat some other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, about this water, did anybody urinate into that water before it was given to you?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No. No. No -- well, maybe. I don't know. But we drank it. I mean, even if somebody had urinated it, maybe we would have had it anyway. We were so thirsty. The temperature was unbearable in there. I mean, I really don't know how come we didn't suffocate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement of the 10th of November, 1995, in paragraph 5, 1D812, you said we had to sing in order to get water but they had urinated into the water that we drank.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what was written down. They wrote that down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But when you testified in the Stakic case, on page 5220, you said that you did not see anyone urinating there. You said that this was just theoretical. And even if someone had urinated into the water you were so thirsty that you would have had it any way.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it's not true that someone urinated into that water?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I cannot assert --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What, that somebody did or did not urinate into that water?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that that is correct. I'm saying that even if someone had done that, we would have had that water nevertheless because we were so thirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you did not see anyone doing that.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Oh, no. No way, I did not see anyone doing that. Now that you've asked me this I have to say something. During those three days we got some bread and these little chocolate balls that's the only thing that we had to eat, now that we're on the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Miska Glava was somebody's name called out? Was somebody taken out? Was somebody killed?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Many names were called out. Among them, my father. I knew most of them, these men who were being taken out. Most of them by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement from the 10th of November, 1998, you do not mention that anybody's names were called out in Miska Glava?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No, that's not the way I had put it. I'm surprised by all these contradictions. I know how many people were taken out and beaten up and never returned. I even know when two men went from this group to bury someone. Now who it was, I don't know. But I mean, I'd just know about this man whose lungs sort of went dead. So there were dead people there too, and they buried someone there by the Dom, since these men went to bury someone. But who it was, I don't know. And I also do not know how many such cases there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when you arrived in the stadium in Ljubija, did you see some people who had already arrived there before you or, rather, you spoke about that a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the stadium in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I had the impression that there were people there when we arrived. When you see lots of people, the stadium is so long, yes. And over there, in Miska Glava, there were already less, so people were taken in this group; apart from those who had been killed individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These men who were standing around you, did they bring someone to point out who it was from your group that had weapons?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were in Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were lined up in front of the stadium?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: By the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now these people with weapons --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they bring some other people to show which people from amongst you had been armed?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, they pointed out this young man and then this young man pointed at someone else, and that's how it was. No, no, no. No. Who was with him somewhere. Not who was armed from amongst us. Now where, was it Kurevo, I don't know. No. Oh, sorry, Lawyer. Can I just go and you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll take a break.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, just five minutes. My bladder is weak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We have to ask the Trial Chamber. Your Honours, may we take a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. The witness can leave the courtroom first and then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As matters stand now, Mr. Traldi, how much time you think you'll need for re-examination, if any at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thus far, very little, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if we would resume at 1.00, do you think that ... again, it's [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Depending on the witness. If he has to make a brief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's not only depending on the witness, as you are aware of. Focussed questioning. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, the Chamber has decided about P1001 and P1002 and has decided that it is appropriate to admit them at this stage of the proceedings. Therefore, P1001 and P1002 are now in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any specific reason why we have to wait -- no, no. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Stakic transcript, on page P233, lines 20 and 21, we need page 30 in e-court of this transcript. You said that you did not know whether a Croat or Muslim had been brought in, one who had been caught in the forest, and he was supposed to point out the persons who were with him in the forest. And then he pointed out two persons, Ismet Avdic and Ferid Kadiric or Kadic?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No, Ferid Kadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said Ferid Kadiric or Kadic.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No way. I did not say that. It can be Ermin Kadic but not Fikret or Ferid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ismet Avdic, Ferid Kadiric. Now we can find this down here in lines 19 through 25. That's what was recorded in this transcript. You're saying today -- actually, do you know who Ferid Kadiric or Kadic is?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Kadiric I should know if we're talking about the first person who was killed in the stadium. If that's the person we're talking about. I should know him, there are two Ferid Kadirics.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: One went into the same class as I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who pointed at weapons?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: He didn't point at anything. And this other one, I don't know. This other Ferid was already by the fence if that's Ferid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about Ismet Avdic?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Ismet Avdic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1D807. Could that be displayed please. That's the statement that you gave on the 11th of November 1992.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: In Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Kindly mention the names of people slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everyone is invited to give names of persons slowly. It's a request on the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I would -- no, we are. Now it's better. I think my voice was -- I tried to activate my microphone but there was wrong. Interpreters have asked everyone to slowly mention names of persons. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement here, the one from Zagreb, around the middle of the page in B/C/S, and on top of the page in the English version, it starts from the second line. You say that he brought Avdic, Ismet; Kadiric, Ferid; and another person to show the persons who had weapons. They indicated 25 persons?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I could not have stated that. I could not have stated that in such form, especially not Ferid Kadiric. I couldn't have mentioned him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have an impression that the official in Zagreb who was taking your statement know -- knew the persons that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No. But I know that they came to the refugee centre to look for me, but I didn't dare stay there any longer. Because of the conflict between the Muslims and Croats, I didn't want to take a chance of being surrendered to the other side. That's why I wanted to go to Germany as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, he treated me well. Let's be clear on that. But I'm not sure that I could have put it in that form.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He could not have written down the name of Ferid Kadiric because he didn't know him, unless it wasn't you who mentioned that. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The official who took the statement, you say that he didn't know the people you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I suppose he wasn't able to know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why I said, unless you mentioned the name of Ferid Kadiric, he wouldn't have noted it down.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know why I mentioned it. And if I did, that was many years ago. It may have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once again, short pause between question and answer and between answer and question. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We now need 1D808 in e-court, please. This is, again, a statement given in Zagreb two months later on the 11th of January, 1993. We need, B/C/S, page 3, and English, page 4. In the B/C/S, it's very at the bottom of the page, and in the English, the very top of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, let go back to this. How it was possible for me to say how many people? I was dead frightened and I couldn't have been counting people --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us just proceed. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please instruct Mr. Mladic to refrain from loud laughter during the testimony of the witness. It will have consequences, as he is aware of and we will not wait for very long. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, you say: "Three traitors attended the questioning."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just tell us where are you reading, Mr. Lukic, please. You said top. Three traitors. What line?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The very top. The first line. Actually, it starts from the second line. Ismet Avdic and further on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, the statement that says "three translators."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might assist. I think in the English the word that appears is informers and it's on the third line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, please, if you allow me. Allow me, please. I see a couple of things here already. Without his reasoning, that -- I don't know. Really, I would discard this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was mention of hats and things of that nature. I don't recall that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, wait -- wait quietly. The only thing we did is the Judges wanted to find the place from where Mr. Lukic was reading. Wait until Mr. Lukic has read what he intends to read, and then he'll put some questions to you, and then you will have an opportunity to say whether you agree or disagree or at least to answer those questions. So just remain quietly, wait for the questions to come, and let Mr. Lukic read first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So did you mention Ismet Avdic, Ferid Kadiric and another man from Carakovo as traitors who betrayed the people who had arms, they were wealthy people and member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: In that respect it is possible. But again you are mentioning Ferid Kadiric and again you are leading me to say that they were traitors. I cannot say that any of them was a traitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm reading what's been noted down.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I had opportunity to read even worse things. Therefore I could kindly ask the Judge not to have this read because I never said them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now have 1D809.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Either I don't remember or I really don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your statement given on the 2nd of May, 1995. B/C/S version, page 3, very top of the page; and English page 4, fourth line from the top. And the sentence begins with the word, "They then ...": "They then singled out three Bosniaks: Avdic, who used to work in a cafe, Ferid Kadiric, and a man from Carakovo, and they were ordered to say who participated in an attempt to free Prijedor and those were members of the Territorial Defence. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No, I don't, if you are asking me about the weapons and whether he was with someone. But as for everything else I discard that completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, who recorded erroneously what you said on four occasions?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Which statement are you talking about? Is it the Zagreb statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The statement of the 2nd of May, 1995. Official is Zijad Ibric.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Judge, I can tell you immediately with regard to this statement and knowing what happened to me later I already was sure that there were some games being played because I signed a lot of things on blank pieces of paper on the assumption that something would be added later. So please bear that in mind when we are discussing these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just briefly, it says here that the witness -- statement was given to SJB Prijedor, MUP of Banja Luka. However, it was given in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Travnik CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now something about how you managed to flee from the bus.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many of you were in the group that remained behind before you jumped out of the bus?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: How many of us remained? Where? On the bus?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: As far as I reckon, not more than five. Do you want me to describe the event?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not necessary. We have it in your statement.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So were there five of you? You said that was not more than five. Was it three? How many?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are trying to get with this, but I'm going to describe the event again, and that's how we will come up with the number. So, when they said the next three, I got up. Somebody -- but what happened during those few seconds, I don't know. I couldn't see everything. All I know is that the one who was taking people out, the driver, was lying on the floor. That Nino from Biscani was lying on to of him holding his rifle. At the same time a window on the left-hand side was broken, and according to some stories later, the one who jumped throughout the window was kill immediately. This is when I turned away to look at the man who was lying on top of the other, and then I see somebody else. A Serb soldier who is pulling the one on top by the legs. At that moment, I went to the window and the one, the guard who was standing there, didn't have any bullets. He was changing his clip. When I jumped out, I went on running. I fell into a hole. I saw three men running past. I didn't know who they were. Only later did I find out who that was. Now, you are asking me to say three, five. One was already killed. Which have two there. We have another one lying on top of the driver. So that's five all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the time of the day when you jumped out of the bus?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: It was moonlight. It was night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you spent the night where?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 150 metres from the place where the shooting took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many -- how -- how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I got up before the break of dawn, and I started walking cautiously. I passed by some tires, I was terribly frightened and I thought that I was too visible because I heard some noise from the forest, so I took off my shoes but my feet were too white so I covered them. And, that I came out and said, shoot me. And that is the moment when I came across the two Croats who told me that everybody from their village had been killed two days before that and that they were looking for women and children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber needs a break of more likely no more than two or three minutes. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom to start with. We will resume, and it will be a very short break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everybody is expected to remain stand-by. And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most likely we're back in two or three minutes. --- Break taken at 1.26 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. The urgent matter the Chamber unfortunately had to deal with is -- has been dealt with by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karagic, the place where you were hiding, did you fall asleep, did you lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Everything could have happened. I remember that I woke up in the morning, and I was cold.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you left there towards Rakovcani?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I said that I saw these two Croats, and they told me to go towards Carakovo because I was not familiar with that ground because I had never been in the forest earlier so I didn't know. And I went in the direction of Carakovo. But before that, many things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who did you meet on the way? A man who was attending cattle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: It is possible. It was an elderly man. He gave me something to eat. Oh, wait. Are you talking about when I was arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Oh. There was an old man -- do I have to say his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have it in the statement.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Is it Avdic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Avdo Dzambastagic. Because you mentioned two Avdos, Avdo and Avdo Dzambastagic. Avdo Avdic and Avdo Dzambastagic.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: That was Avdo Dzambastagic. Somebody wrote it wrongly. He was sitting there and tending cows.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then a uniformed person with a beard came and arrested you?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then another man in the reserve police uniform came.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And they arrested you there. So what happened next?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: They took me, I think I was put in a car. They were speaking about fuel while they were outside, and I thought that that could give me a chance to escape. They took me out of the car and put me on a tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How much fuel did you tell them you had?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know that I said how much fuel I had. I only said I have fuel at that moment. Or at least I think so. Well, and, Lawyer, yes, I did have fuel. But I sincerely wanted to bring them to the fuel but my real intention was to escape. So when they took me to my house, we were building a large storage for fruit and vegetables, and some of it is still preserved below the ground and what is above the ground is derelict. And I think that there were blocks prepared for further building, and fuel was inside. And that occurred to me when I told them I had fuel. However, when -- we came there, somebody had already found the fuel. I don't know how, but it was gone. So I took them behind the stable because I had another hiding place, and I found a barrel with 20 litres of fuel. I wanted to flee then, but this man was guarding me at gun point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to these people about the quantities of oil that you could give them?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Uh-huh, later. I don't know whether it was exactly those people. I know that when I was burying the dead in Rizvanovici, that -- now how did that happen? I think that I thought that I could buy my own life back by giving fuel. I know when this guy hit me, well, first with some piece of wood. I mean, somebody had found -- I don't know how to say this. It was a big piece of wood, and he hit me with that, and I said, How much is my life worth? And he said, 5.000 litres of fuel. And I said, Well, I have 200. I just happened to remember that my uncle had some buried somewhere. I have no idea. But this just sort of happened to go through my head, and, yeah. Well, possibly. Possibly. When -- when -- when he already had that stake that he wanted to impale me on and he said, Fuck you. Why didn't you tell me immediately? And he wanted to hit me and I caught this in the air. I don't know. I don't know. Whether he got me or I got him, out of fear, I mean, I would never let go. Never let go. I was hoping that the commander would help. So I called the commander. I said, Commander, commander, so that he would help me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So did he help you? Did anyone help?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was somebody lying there on you, pretending to beat you but was actually protecting you?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. And later on, I think that he let me -- well, I don't know. I'm not glad to be saying this, because of this man. In fact he saved me from that soldier who wanted to impale me on that stake. But now did he have the intention of helping me? He did do it though. He was playing with this knife walking up to me, and he sort of fell. And that moment I was fleeing and he had nothing to trip over. I mean, it was just a clearing, a meadow. I think that he fell on purpose, to give me the chance to run away. Well, that would be it. I know that I was supposed to bury six others before I ran away. Well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did someone fire at you?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: As I ran to the brook, I just heard something fly by me, and I saw later on that it was a grenade that exploded. I thought that it had blown away my ear and I was holding onto my ear and I was also wounded by it, here. Now I don't know whether there's any shrapnel left anywhere. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're showing your hand. The wound -- your hand or head?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Here, here. I thought that it had fallen off but it was just grazed, here. But it was sort of -- they weren't shooting then. I think. I think. They just fired and then later on I'd find out -- I mean, I didn't have experience with this military stuff. I mean, you know the thing that they call drunken Ustashas, you know. It's like a rifle grenade, sort of something that's round and then you put a grenade there and then, well, it was with that that they fired this grenade. I saw that soldier, but I didn't know what this was used for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D812. Could we briefly take a look at that now, please. We need page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your statement of the 10th of November, 1998. We need paragraph 15. Page 5, both versions. This is what you say here in the English version. It is the sixth line from the top.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I've read that before you did. So this text is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait for the question to be put.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I'm sorry. But I've read the entire paragraph so I know what's written there so I wanted to tell him straight away that that's the way it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just wait for the question. That is what we expect you to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is what is written here: "A Serb fired at me and I thought I was dead but he only hit my shirt, not me."

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Correct as I was burying those two, he was playing with me, shooting at me before he went to get the stake sharpened for impaling me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It wasn't before the escape.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No, no, it was before we started wrestling. Is that the word you use, wrestling? At any rate, we were both holding that and... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when were you asked whether you were hungry and did they offer you any food?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: To the Bosna cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And they gave you something to eat there?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand in terms of time when this happened. I mean, in relation to this preparing the stake and holding onto it.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour or two later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After you were holding the stake and wrestling?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No. First, I mean, remember that paragraph? That's where it's written. All of it. Before that, they took me to the cafe. I mean, first, the thing with the belt. And then I ended up at the cafe. And then in the cafe I was questioned by this commander. And I had to -- I address him as the commander of Serbian Biscani, Rakovcani, and as I spoke to him, he put a pile of IDs in front of me. I really didn't know any of these people. I just recognised the waiter. Out of all of these IDs that were there. And they all come from my village. But there you go. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: And then this man was sort of poking at me with his knife. They offered me a cigarette. However, since this guy was sort of poking me with that knife, I sort of said I couldn't. Whereas this guy said, Fuck you, eat. And then well, that would be it. And then I said -- now what was this that I said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Wait for --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. We really have to move on because our time is limited. We're trying to finish today so that you don't have to come back tomorrow. So I will just have a few more questions. After that this one is pretending to beat you, and then you are haggling over the stake, and now where -- where did you arrive after that, when you were fleeing from these people?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I know that I first ran into a thicket and then I lay there, and then they ran by me, ran by me. Then they went further on to look for me, and I went in the opposite direction. In fact, I was going through the open -- I mean, there were these raspberries that were planted in rows and then there was some kind of path that was open, and I saw this path and I managed to squeeze through. It was short of like a path. You know how thicket is when you are moving through raspberries. At any rate, I managed to escape, they were looking for me in the forest, and I was running in the opposite direction. Now where did I arrive? I arrived in Rika. That's what we call it. There was this little house. And I walked into that house and I kept holding my ear, right? And then I entered that house, and -- and, sorry. Sorry. Sorry. Since they called me Green Beret, I found a green -- a -- a green sheet and I thought, Oh, fuck, they're going to kill me now. And I found this knife. And then I took it with me. And then the third time when they noticed me I wanted to kill myself with that very same knife. At any rate I did not want to be caught alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That time, when you hid, did you ever pass out as you were running? Did you ever hit your head?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, there. But not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Kipe is when you jumped out of the bus?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Well, when I ran, that's where I passed out, if I did pass out. I just know that I woke up in the morning. Well, look, for a few days we hadn't slept. Now we were there for how many days and we did not really sleep when they were taken prisoner. I don't think that anybody felt like sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you ever hiding in a tree?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: A tree? I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I know I was underneath a tree. I had this hole dug there, and I know that I hid there for quite a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us briefly take a look at transcript ... actually, the Stakic transcript. We need page 65. In e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I need a page number. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is what you say here. Yes. 5268; that's the page number from the Stakic transcript. I'm going to read it out in English so that you get the right interpretation. From line 16 onwards: [In English] "There was slope there, and I took out the cord off my shorts, which I then tied to a tree there. And I tied myself to the tree so that they wouldn't see me. I was hanging upside down, actually, and they were not very far from me."

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: It is correct. It is correct. I've already told you that. I wanted to kill myself then. I was holding the knife -- the knife and I took the cord out of those Hawaii short, whatever you call them, and then tied it to the fence. How could I tie it to the tree? And then on one side there were cows and on the other side were leaves. And they passed by me and they went to look for me further. Now where this thing, hanging upside down came from, I really have no idea. And then I was holding this knife --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you did not say that you were hanging upside down with your head down?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No. How could I do that? I don't know how come that's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, you joined this group of people who were supposed to go to Travnik; is that right? And that's were you found your brother; right?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Some of these people were armed as well, when you found them; right?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Two of them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly repeat his last answer, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your last answer. You were asked: "Some of these people were armed as well, when you found them; right?" And then the answer which is recorded was: "Yes. Two of them." Did you say anything further or was that your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let us briefly go back to what you said. You said that you signed these empty sheets of paper?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was it that you signed these empty sheets of paper, in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: The CSB Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Zagreb, I don't remember what happened there. I don't remember. But I know that I gave a statement and -- I don't know. I don't think that such -- I don't know. I don't think I said such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very briefly. You were in Germany. And you came from Germany via Mostar, as you said, to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you come with a group of fighters?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in Germany, did you undergo any kind of military training?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No. With the approval of the German authorities, I left. I asked them to let me go. I couldn't take it anymore. I often had dreams of what had happened to me. And then, also due to certain emotional matters -- I mean, I met this girl --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We understand that. Can you just tell us how many blank papers were given to you in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During all these years --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, there is a video recording as well, so maybe on the basis of this video recording can show what I said exactly. There was a camera on while I was giving my statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Over the years --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will have to go to private session for a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, this concluded your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, thank you for answering my questions. This is all I wanted to ask you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It will be about five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, at temporary transcript, page 56, Mr. Lukic asked you whether you were lined up Ljubija stadium in two lines or four lines. And could we have 1D00812, page 3, paragraph 5, the statement that Mr. Lukic showed you. And once that comes up - again 1D00812, page 3 - I would just ask you to take a moment, review that paragraph that he showed you, and tell the Judges whether you were discussing the Ljubija stadium at that point or you were discussing the time that you were captured.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. Paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, I touched it with my finger unintentionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps it would help if I pointed you --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: So what's unclear about it? Everything stands as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm asking you a very simp question. Mr. Lukic suggested to you that at this point you were talking about the lines at the stadium and I'm asking you were you in fact in this paragraph talking about being put into the four lines when you were captured in the forest.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Correct, correct. That is where the four lines were. Good of you to remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it was the stadium where you were put into two lines, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at different times during cross-examination, Mr. Lukic asked you about armed resistance at Hambarine and suggested some of the victims at the Ljubija stadium were in the Territorial Defence. I have only two focussed questions for you in this respect. First, beginning when your group was taken to Miska Glava Dom --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, can you please repeat what you just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At some points during cross-examination, Mr. Lukic asked you about fighting in Hambarine; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. But he mentioned the wrong day when he was speaking about it. I could only have spoken about this initial attack on the check-point, but not on the attack the following day. I could only have spoken about the shells hitting the houses because I was able to see that from the town. I was running to the Rizvanovici check-point, and I was able to see from there where the shells were landing. As for the other thing, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I only have two very focussed questions. From -- beginning when your group was taken to Miska Glava Dom and ending at the time that you escaped from the bus, did you see anyone in your group holding a weapon?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you at all. I am confused. Can you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure, and I'll take it very slowly. Your group was captured in the forest and then taken to Miska Glava Dom; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So from that point when you got to the Dom, through when you were taken to the stadium and on the bus to Kipe, in that entire time, did you see anyone in your group holding a weapon?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC
utterances.text: No, no. Nobody. They didn't even have ID cards or money. Everything had been seized from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that completes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. The Bench has no further questions for you. Mr. Lukic, I see that the re-examination has not triggered any need for any further questions. Mr. Karagic, this concludes your testimony in this Court. We'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and we wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm sorry for all these things that I don't understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In -- is there any matter remaining? I don't think so. There's the chart. Is still -- Mr. Lukic, are you already in a position, or would you rather take your time before you express the final opinion about the chart?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would rather take my time. So if I analyse it properly, maybe I can change my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give us a time estimate on how much time it would take you to analyse it properly? Is that a matter of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's even more than I expected. So we'll hear from you early next week. Let's say not later than by Tuesday. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll deal with that. I have a few matters which I would like to raise in the few remaining minutes. First, in an e-mail of the 20th of February, the Chamber was informed of an agreement between the parties to replace Exhibit D124, under seal, with a redacted version of the same document and that was due to restrictions on this document pursuant to Rule 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I just wondered whether I had ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The exhibit number is correct and the reason is correct as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the next matter I'd like to deal with is MFI D1 ... Yes, Madam Registrar, you are hereby instructed to replace the unredacted version of D124 by the redacted version. The next item deals with D198, MFI'd. Defence Exhibit 198 was MFI'd on the 8th of February during the testimony of Anthony Banbury due to a missing translation. In e-mail of the 20th of February, 2013, the Defence notified the Chamber that it had uploaded a translation into e-court under doc ID 1D02-3163. Madam Registrar, you are hereby instructed to attach the translation to MFI D198, and the Chamber admits into evidence D198 under seal. Next item concerns Defence Exhibit 170, marked for identification, with Witness RM009. D170 was MFI'd during the testimony of Witness RM009 on the 4th of February of this year due to the lack of an English translation. This is to be found at transcript page 8033. In an e-mail of the 20th of February, the Defence notified the Chamber that it had uploaded an English translation in e-court under doc ID 1D02-3164. Madam Registrar, the Chamber hereby instructs you to attach the translation to D170, and the Chamber admits D170 into evidence, under seal. Any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Defence has nothing today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let me ... Then we will adjourn, and I lost my little note, but it will be until Monday. We adjourn until Monday, the 25th of February, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of February, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.
